newsitem.title: USA: Rawlings sees Q4 ahead of year-ago results.
newsitem.headline: Rawlings sees Q4 ahead of year-ago results.

text.p: Rawlings Sporting Goods Co Inc said it expected increased revenues and earnings in its fiscal fourth quarter ending August 31, compared with its results in the comparable prior-year quarter.

"The recovery of retail sales of baseball-related products continues to be somewhat sluggish," Chief Executive Carl Shields said. "However, Rawlings continues to gain market share in several key baseball-related categories and is well positioned to benefit from further recovery of baseball."
The company on Monday reported earnings for the third quarter ended May 31 of $0.26 per share, up 18.2 percent from the year-earlier quarter.

Improved third-quarter earnings mainly reflected higher revenues, lower selling, general and administrative (SG&A) expenses, and lower interest expense, partially offset by a lower gross margin, Rawling said.
"The results achieved in the third quarter were generally in line with our expectations," Shields said.
Net revenues in the quarter ended May 31 were $39.9 million, up 1.9 percent over a year ago.

"Improved net revenues from inflatables (basketballs, footballs and volleyballs) and apparel partially offset by lower net revenues from baseball-related products and licensing were primarily responsible for the increase," Rawlings said.
Gross margin on the quarter was 31.6 percent, a half percentage point lower than the gross margin of 32.1 percent in the comparable quarter last year.

"The lower gross margin was primarily the result of lower licensing revenues related to a domestic licensee. This licensee has indicated that it expects its results related to Rawlings' licensed product to improve in the fiscal fourth quarter," the company said.
SG&A expenses were $8.5 million on the quarter, down 2.9 percent from a year ago, while interest expense was $864,000, or 12.2 percent lower than the comparable prior-year quarter.
